items.item_text: 01. All applicants are required to submit responses to the following supplemental questions. Your responses will provide information about your background and experience related to this position and will be used in the screening and selection process. Be concise yet specific and informative in your responses to these supplemental questions. "See resume," attachments or links will not be accepted as a substitute for your responses to the questions in the following boxes. Incomplete responses will not be considered. Please indicate below that you have read and understand these instructions. Options: Yes | No

02. I understand that my application will be considered incomplete if any required sections of the application are not completed and/or if any documents that are required are not attached to my online application by the closing date. Options: Yes | No
03. Please specify your highest level of education. Options: High School or equivalent (GED) | Associate's Degree | Bachelor's Degree | Master's Degree | Juris Doctor | Doctorate Degree
04. Please indicate the field in which you have earned your degree in:

05. Please indicate the number of years of experience you have of formal training or leadership experience reasonably related to the administrator's administrative assignment. Options: No experience | Less than one year | One Year | Two Years | Three Years | Four Years | Five Years or more

06. Indicate where you obtained at least two (2) years of formal training or leadership experience reasonably related to the administrator’s assignment. 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed. (This section is required)
07. Do you have experience teaching in a California Community College? Options: Yes | No
08. Do you have experience with accelerated Instruction? Options: Yes | No

09. Which of the following best describes your experience overseeing instructional operations, including class scheduling, faculty assignments, enrollment management, FTES goals, and instructional budgets? Options: No experience overseeing instructional operations. | Limited experience assisting with or coordinating instructional operations. Limited experience assisting with or coordinating instructional operations. | Experience directly managing one or two instructional operations, such as scheduling, faculty assignments, or budgets. | Substantial experience managing several instructional operations, including scheduling, faculty assignments, enrollment management, or budgets. | Extensive experience overseeing multiple instructional operations, including scheduling, faculty assignments, FTES goals, and instructional budgets.

10. If you indicated that you have experience overseeing instructional operations, please provide the following information: 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed.

11. Which of the following best describes your experience developing, implementing, or modifying instructional programs and curriculum, including ensuring compliance with applicable educational regulations and guidelines? Options: No experience in instructional program or curriculum development. | Limited experience assisting with instructional program or curriculum development. | Experience participating in the development, implementation, or modification of instructional programs or curriculum. | Substantial experience directly overseeing instructional program or curriculum development, including collaboration with faculty and ensuring compliance with applicable guidelines. | Extensive experience leading the development, implementation, and modification of multiple instructional programs or curricula, including ensuring compliance with applicable educational regulations and guidelines.

12. If you indicated that you have experience developing, implementing, or modifying instructional programs or curriculum, please provide the following information: 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed.

13. Which of the following best describes your experience overseeing program reviews, assessing learning outcomes, analyzing institutional data, and using assessment results to support instructional planning and program improvement? Options: No experience with program assessment, data analysis, or institutional planning. | Limited experience assisting with program reviews, learning outcomes assessments, or institutional data analysis. | Experience conducting program reviews, assessing learning outcomes, or analyzing data to inform instructional decisions. | Substantial experience overseeing program reviews and learning outcomes assessments and using data to guide instructional planning and program improvements. | Extensive experience leading program reviews, learning outcomes assessments, and data-driven institutional planning initiatives that resulted in demonstrated instructional improvements or improved student outcomes.

14. If you indicated that you have experience with program assessment, data analysis, or institutional planning, please provide the following information: 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed.

15. Which of the following best describes your experience collaborating with faculty, staff, administrators, and student services personnel to facilitate shared governance, institutional planning, and initiatives that support student success? Options: No experience with collaborative leadership or shared governance. | Limited experience participating in collaborative meetings, committees, or institutional initiatives. | Experience actively participating in shared governance committees or collaborative initiatives involving faculty, staff, or administrators. | Substantial experience leading committees or collaborative initiatives involving multiple institutional departments or constituent groups. | Extensive experience leading shared governance efforts and cross-departmental initiatives, facilitating collaborative decision-making, and implementing initiatives that resulted in demonstrated improvements in instructional programs, student services, or student success.

16. If you indicated that you have experience with collaborative leadership, shared governance, or cross-departmental initiatives, please provide the following information: 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed.
17. Please indicate a demonstrated ability to articulate a meaningful commitment to the college's identity and mission. This section is required.

18. Describe how you have demonstrated sensitivity and understanding in delivery of services and support to a diverse workforce and student population (diverse in terms of socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic background). This section is required.
19. I have completed all sections of the application including references. (Statements such as "see resume" will not be acceptable.) Options: Yes | No

Coordinate the educational operations and activities of the assigned division including developing class schedules, generating faculty assignments, and projecting and meeting Full Time Equivalent Student (FTES) enrollment targets
In consultation with departments within the division, prepare and monitor program budgets
Support faculty in the development and assessment of Student Learning Outcomes (SLOs), Program Learning Outcomes (PLOs), and Institutional Learning Outcomes (ILOs)
Work with faculty to ensure completion of division program reviews
Participate fully in the integrated planning process
Ensure that programs operate within State and Federally-mandated requirements
Work with faculty and staff to determine needs for curriculum or program additions, modifications, and deletions
Prepare documents/reports for program and course development, including accurate schedules, catalog information and support of program publicity

Maintain current knowledge of new developments, to include changes in information technology impacting online teaching, and curriculum and articulation requirements in community colleges and higher education
Work cooperatively with Student Affairs personnel to analyze data from assessment and testing methods and practices relevant to course/program offerings
Partner with and support Student Services by informing faculty of programs and services (e.g. EOPS, DSPS, Veterans, Foster Youth, CalWORKs, Ujima) available to students
Consult collegially with faculty and staff regarding appropriate schedule of classes to meet the needs of students

Determine final schedule, faculty assignments, and substitute assignments; monitor schedules and workload for accuracy throughout the semester including timely submission of schedules and final grades
Follow provisions of collective bargaining agreements
Administer financial resources consistent with District policy
Develop and maintain external relationships with applicable departments, divisions, or schools at local four year institutions
Evaluate and approve requests for supplies and equipment, maintaining consistent communication with departments

Communicate with faculty and staff by holding regular meetings and in-service training to facilitate collaborative planning and decision-making; keep them informed about College-wide issues and projects
Collaboratively determine needs for staff and faculty development, and facilitate record-keeping to ensure staff and faculty development accountability

Organize and serve on committees for hiring and ensure compliance with District personnel policies, procedures and practices for the employment of faculty, administrators, classified staff, student workers and short-term temporary and substitute employees
Mediate and resolve faculty, staff and student problems, complaints and first level grievances according to employee contracts and College policy and procedures

Supervise and evaluate faculty, classified staff, and auxiliary personnel according to proper management practices, District policies and procedures, the Collective Bargaining contracts, and state and federal regulations
Serve on College and ad hoc committees and participate in campus-wide and community activities; actively engage in shared governance with all constituents and foster collaborative relationships
Represent the District in local, regional and state-wide instructional meetings and committees, which may include travel
Perform other related duties as assigned

Interpret and apply a variety of rules, regulations, policies, and guidelines including Federal and state legislation, and California Education Code

Effectively counsel and assist staff, faculty, administrators, and the public
The California Education Code, Title 5 and other state, federal, and local laws, regulations, restrictions and requirements as they apply to the community college
Review and analyze data for accuracy and completeness and make recommendations
California Community College Chancellor’s Office guidelines
Research and assist in resolving issues involving data fields contained within specialized software

This is primarily a sedentary office classification although standing and walking between work areas may be required.
Office productivity software such as Microsoft, Word, Excel, Outlook, Access
Additionally, this position requires occasional independent travel by car to visit various District and meeting sites.
Modern office procedures, practices and equipment
Positions in this classification occasionally bend, stoop, kneel, reach, push, and pull drawers open and closed to retrieve and file information.
Budget preparation and management
Employees work in an office environment with moderate noise levels, controlled temperature conditions, and no direct exposure to hazardous physical substances.
Standard management principles and practices of effective administration, supervision, and training
Employees may interact with upset students, faculty, staff and/or public and private representatives when interpreting and enforcing departmental policies and procedures.

Communicate effectively both orally and in writing
Establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with others; use interpersonal skills such as tact, patience, courtesy, and diplomacy
Ability to multitask at varying levels of detail
Operate a computer and various software programs; navigate the Internet

Demonstrate clear evidence of sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, faculty, staff and community

Must possess mobility to work in a standard office setting and use standard office equipment, including a computer; vision to read printed materials and a computer screen; and hearing and speech to communicate in person, before groups, and over the telephone.
Finger dexterity is needed to access, enter, and retrieve data using a computer keyboard or calculator and to operate standard office equipment.
Employees must possess the ability to lift, carry, push, and pull materials and objects up to 25 pounds when using proper techniques and devices.
